ai.description: The Assam Tree Frog (Rhacophoridae) measures 5–7 cm. It is olive-green or brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale belly. Key features include translucent webbing and a distinct white subocular spot.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates assamensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged, cream-colored lateral stripe that extends from the snout through the eye to the flank.
ai.habitat: The Assam Tree Frog inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The Assam Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among the foliage of its humid, forested habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates assamensis* breeds during the monsoon (May–August), depositing foam nests containing approximately 150–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assam Tree Frog is found in Northeast India, specifically across Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting tropical forests at elevations between 200 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Assam Tree Frog emits a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near stagnant water pools during the monsoon season.
